page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, with 4 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 60.0 GB of RAM, a local 472 GB SSD for storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance split between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 CPU exhibits weak single-core and multi-core performance in stress-ng and Passmark tests, placing in the bottom 10% to 25% relative to newer hardware. Similarly, memory bandwidth and database operations show lower-tier performance. However, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU delivers strong results in LLM inference benchmarks, achieving top-tier performance for prompt processing on 135M and 7B models, as well as text generation on 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a budget-friendly entry point for GPU-accelerated computing, trading off raw CPU and memory speed for dedicated GPU resources. It is highly suitable for small-to-medium LLM inference, legacy CUDA-based machine learning workloads, and static web serving. It is less suited for CPU-heavy compilation, high-throughput database operations, or memory-bandwidth-bound applications.

It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor, 60.0 GB of RAM, a 472 GB local SSD, and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Graphics and compute acceleration are handled by a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. While CPU-bound benchmarks and memory bandwidth tests place this instance in the lower performance tiers, its GPU capabilities deliver top-tier results in LLM inference for small and medium models. This hardware profile makes the instance a cost-effective choice for machine learning inference, legacy CUDA applications, and static web serving, though it is less optimal for CPU-intensive or high-throughput database tasks.
